$comparability.why: This file was measured against the previous golden set, which is not a golden set: 33 of its 100 protocols are not what the published stratified rule produces from the committed 159-document corpus, 95 of 95 protocols had drifted, 0 of 260 rules carried a snapshot id or a character offset, and 10 probes were unreachable in the section they named. node eval/build-golden.mjs did not reproduce it. These numbers are NOT comparable to any run made against eval/golden.json.
what_changed_in_the_instrument: RECALL is now reported under a BOUNDED matcher (the emitted row may not exceed the probe by more than 1.5x) beside the containment matcher that was used here; both are in every new results file.
RECALL is now reported beside its own FLOOR (three deliberately trivial extractors) and marked VOID where the floor beats it.
VERIFY is now one number per verdict condition, not one pooled percentage of the store against itself.
CALLS is now over three divisors, with the harness auditing calls separated from the calls a caller pays.
NEGATIVE PROBES and CONSERVATION are new; neither has a counterpart in this file.
$comparability.supersedes_note: Nothing in this file is wrong about the build it measured. It is simply measured against a set that cannot be rebuilt, and a number without a rebuildable denominator is an anecdote with decimals.

$comment: Hand review of every BEFORE miss, so a recall number is not read as a defect count.
The harness cannot do this: whether a missed sentence binds an implementer is a
judgement, and the point of the bench is that the judgement is made against the RFC
text rather than against the tool's behaviour.
tool_defect      - the sentence binds an implementer and the tool did not return it
probe_artifact   - the tool returned the statement; the probe over-captured it
label_error      - the sentence does not bind an implementer, or the probe is not
one; this is a fault in the bench, not in the tool
unreachable_class- a keyword-free specification, which no keyword-driven pass can find

totals.note: totals describe the BEFORE run and do not move. Verdicts were re-examined on 2026-09-26 against the current build by eval/results/strict-miss-diagnosis.md: 2 were never misses in that build (closed), 2 carried wrong attributions (re-attributed with a mechanism), 4 are tool defects with a localised mechanism.

corrected_recall.rule: A miss counts against recall only when the sentence binds an implementer and the tool returned it nowhere. `probe_artifact` means the tool DID return the statement and the probe over-captured it, so it moves to the numerator. `label_error` and `unreachable_class` leave the denominator.

misses.why: A flattened table of transfer-type defaults. The last clause ('All hosts must accept the above as the standard defaults') is a real obligation, but the probe is the table, and the tool is right to skip a table.
'Each node has a set of resource information, which may be empty.' Describes the protocol; nothing is required of an implementer.
A field definition with no modal token.

Upper-case SHOULD, and it was found - in non_strict_candidates, with reason `non_prose_block`. The block was classified preformatted because RFC 1122 indents its body text at column 12. `coverage.total_requirements` said 17 while the same text yielded 255 upper-case modal-and-demand candidates. This is the defect the prose-classification fix removes.
States a timeout (4 minutes) with no modal token.
States a give-up time (4-5 days) with no modal token.

Upper-case MUST in a listed section. Mechanism localised 2026-09-26: a page break ends the block mid-sentence, splitSentences runs per block, so the strict pass emits the first half as a complete requirement. 274 corpus rows in 38 documents are page-break first halves, 220 unflagged. See eval/results/pending-fixes.md Y1.
A real MUST NOT inside a block that also holds a numbered encoding table, so the block is not prose. Part of the table limitation, not of the indent defect.
'WebNFS clients ... should use READDIRPLUS in preference to READDIR.' The document yields ONE candidate in total, so the prose fix should return it.
'The effects on security of not implementing a MUST or SHOULD ... may be very subtle.' RFC 2119 discussing its own keywords. A miss here is not a gap in a contract.
The probe is a list of reserved TLDs plus a sentence about one of them. Structural.
A real upper-case MAY in a 1993 RFC whose body is set as a table of options. Open; the option table is the blocker.
